result.title: The Dynamics of Collapse and Recovery in Clustered Federated Learning
result.summary: Clustered federated learning (CFL) can suffer from cluster collapse. In particular, under unfavorable initialization, early client assignments concentrate heterogeneous groups on one cluster model, which is then trained toward a pooled compromise, while another model receives no updates. Since the current models determine client routing and routing determines subsequent model updates, we formulate clustered federated learning as control of an unknown dynamical system, with cluster models as the evolving state, client routing patterns as the control input, and routing interventions as state dependent controllers. In a two group linear model, we identify an initialization region in which greedy routing makes collapse self reinforcing. We then derive finite horizon error dynamics showing how routing interventions can reverse collapse by repeatedly training the starved model, primarily with updates from its compatible group. Motivated by this condition, each client uses blocked EXP3 to choose between greedy routing and interventions that redirect updates toward unused models. Experiments show that with simpler predictors and faster specialist formation, autonomous controller selection recovers usable specialists from unfavorable starts that trap standard CFL baselines. In transformed FEMNIST, the synchronized-entry configuration with persistent commitment recovers usable specialists in settings where the autonomous controller configuration often does not. Code and scripts for reproducing the experiments and figures are available at https://github.com/prsinha1/FedRecover.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究聚类联邦学习中的「簇坍塌」，把簇模型视为状态、客户端路由视为控制输入，在两组线性模型下刻画导致坍塌自增强的初始化区域与有限时域误差动力学，并提出基于 blocked EXP3 的路由干预选择以从未良初始化中恢复可用专家。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态—控制输入—坍塌/恢复」的问题表述可能可用于类比 LVR 中并行或循环 latent 假设塌缩为折中表示、以及自适应干预与停止决策的刻画，但跨领域迁移需核查。
